tasks.title: Collect every Indus-inscribed object found outside the Indus region
tasks.summary: 55 foreign Indus-inscribed objects listed (4 new to us, none with a usable sequence yet; 41 with >=2 legible signs) in experiments/foreign_corpus/foreign_corpus.csv. 10/39 scorable texts break Indus order by the Wells grammar (2.0 expected, binomial p=1.6e-5; 7/22 round/cylinder, 2/7 square), 11 borderline; 3 of these have disputed reading direction.

tasks.title: Build the name list for owners of seals found abroad
tasks.summary: Built names.csv (7,776 names, 7,066 syllabified; ORACC epsd2/names + oldbab + rimanum, CDLI Ur III seals, 473 Gulf co-text names) plus short crib lists: short_gulf_core.csv (21 Meluhha/Magan/Dilmun people + 6 Gulf deities) and top-150 per language. Only 2 names (na-na-sa, sa-mar) are securely non-Mesopotamian; Sumerian/Akkadian/Amorite names repeat a syllable less than chance (0.096/0.085/0.042 vs null 0.139/0.101/0.123), mean 3.5-3.9 syllables.

tasks.title: Design and validate the crib attack on planted data (no Indus data yet)
tasks.summary: With planted Ur III names in a simulated syllabic script (20% misreading, frames, 25% name-free texts) the crib attack against a 6.7k-spelling list has power 0.00/0.40/0.10/0.50 at n=20/30/60/120 and recovers 2-4% of sign values; even the TRUE key scores below the 95th pct of keys fitted to shuffled texts at every n<=120 (e.g. 38 vs 71 at n=20). Feasible only with short per-site name lists, anchors, an exact-match score (true-key unicity between n=60 and 120), or more texts; redesigned prereg draft in experiments/crib_attack/prereg_real_draft.md.

tasks.title: Run the crib attack on the real foreign corpus
Bench the May 2026 Proto-Dravidian key (185 signs)
tasks.summary: The 185-reading Proto-Dravidian key does not beat its own shuffled readings on held-out M77 (Tamil-bigram hit 0.547 vs null 0.491, p=0.16; junction p=0.11; dictionary p=0.75), and keys fitted to shuffled sign strings reach 0.97 bigram hit. Its 92.8% coverage is frequency-only (74.1% on M77 both real and token-shuffled) and its Uniform 0.0% baseline is a case artefact (fair uniform 27%); caveat: planted test shows S1/S2 lack power at this size.

tasks.title: Bench the other 2026 claims: 'convergent Dravidian' key and the registration-code reading
tasks.summary: Kriger&Hunt registration-code signatures fail on 646 Mohenjo-daro unicorn seals: texts are LESS unique than chance (88.2% vs 97.5-99.2% under nulls), numerals do not favour the penultimate slot (p=0.46), their dominant '2' is the M99 connective (27.7% without it), and 20/80 near-duplicate pairs differ at edges (p=0.06 vs positional null, absent on other seals); only the long-known edge-entropy pattern replicates, which SIGIL shows is non-specific. Adelman's convergent-Dravidian key is behind an Academia.edu login, so no sign table could be benched.

tasks.title: Graffiti beside Tamil-Brahmi: get the data and run the power gate
tasks.summary: The open 2026 TN catalogue (Rajan & Sivanantham, 1,570 Tamil-Brahmi sherds) flags only 20 secure sherds with both a Tamil-Brahmi text and a graffiti mark (Kodumanal 5, Keeladi 5, Alagankulam 5, Arikamedu 2, Korkai 2, Marungur 1), and none of the 20 marks is identified to a sign, so the gate (>=30) is not passed and no test was run. Power of the preregistered Holm-Fisher test at n=20 is only 0.25 (OR 3) to 0.57 (OR 10); about 60 identified sherds give 0.94-0.97 at OR 10; descriptively the mark sits at the word's end in 16 of 18 placed cases.

tasks.title: Sign meaning classes from deciphered scripts: feasibility and held-out-script gate
tasks.summary: Held-out-script gate FAILED: a model trained on two read scripts (ORACC Old Akkadian-period admin, TLA Egyptian, EDH Latin; 2,300 units each) to label NAME/CONTENT/FUNC from position/partner/frequency features reached macro-F1 0.43/0.36/0.38, beating frequency alone by +0.12 everywhere but beating the shuffled-label null only for Latin (p = 0.035; Egyptian p = 0.065, cuneiform p = 0.26). Pre-registered rule required all three, so no classes were assigned to Indus signs.

tasks.title: Sweep 2024-2026 research for methods and data we have not used
tasks.summary: 18 items from 2024-2026 checked against the atlas: no new bilingual or text beside Indus signs; one new foreign-found Indus-sign seal (Umm al-Quwain, UAE, about Apr 2026, aggregator only). Added 5 tasks: UAE seal into the foreign corpus, a Linear Elamite known-answer test for the crib attack, bench of the IIT Hyderabad restoration release (Zenodo 24164070), a test of Dominik's W520/W740-W090 claim, and a red team of the ivc2tyc Tibetan-Yi similarity.

tasks.title: Are the foreign texts structurally names? Compare with real seal legends
tasks.summary: 40 foreign texts are nearest Akkadian personal names by edge/repeat shape (z-distance 1.78, power 0.81 at n=40) but are equally compatible with home Indus seals (D 3.08, not rejected), so shape does not show they are names; Ur III legends, Sumerian and Amorite names are rejected (shared-initial 0.70/0.78 vs 0.375, p<0.001). No recurring theophoric suffix: the final slot is the ordinary closer W740 (7/40), while numerals sit text-final abroad unusually often (21% of numeral tokens vs 5.5% at home, descriptive).

tasks.title: Red-team #1: are the 10 'non-Indus order' foreign texts real or reading/direction artefacts?
tasks.summary: Claim holds: 9/39 foreign texts stay out of Indus order under every direction and alternative reading (exp 1.95, p=1.1e-4) and beat a one-misreading null (exp 2.9, p=0.002); flags are order-driven (permutation q median 0.51 vs native 0, p=1e-7) except SALUT-01. SUSA-02 drops (its M77 reading scores Indus-like, p=0.25) while UR-02 (M77 ending, p=0.005), FAILAKA-01 reversed (p=0.02) and UR-05 (M77, p=0.04) become flagged.

tasks.title: Check the readings of the foreign texts against published drawings/photos
tasks.summary: Partial check. Gadd 1932 (open on archive.org) corrects 4 identities: ICIT 3887 = M77 9902 (Gadd 18, double-counted; Gadd's text supports the M77 5-sign reading), M77 9842 = Gadd 12 pictorial device (excluded), M77 9845 = Laursen no.20 (duplicate), Gadd 4 reading conflict; Gadd 16 has 4 signs not 6. Dedup re-run: 9/38 foreign objects break Indus order (1.9 expected, p=8.5e-5); readings_check.csv marks 9 objects to use in #4, but no sign-by-sign check was possible (halftones; Parpola 1994b, CISI 3.1, Amiet, Kjaerum not found open).

tasks.title: Identify the 20 graffiti marks on Tamil-Brahmi sherds and add Sri Lankan sherds to reach n>=30
tasks.summary: From the 2026 catalogue's printed photos, only 2 of the 21 marks beside Tamil-Brahmi can be named at grade B (a sign-40 triangle at Kodumanal, a figure at Alagankulam); 5 are guesses and 14 are illegible, and the one Sri Lankan source (Falk 2014) needs a login, so n stays far below 30 and the hashed test is not run. Side finding: on 2 of 21 sherds the Appendix I reading and the plate caption disagree, so the #7 count of 20 carries about a 10% error.

tasks.title: Meaning-class gate with genre-matched seal-legend corpora (reopen of #8)
tasks.summary: Genre-matched corpora (Ur III seal legends from ORACC ur3 with POS, 6,467; Egyptian verbless phrases, 2,640; Latin labels/stamps, 1,833): the power check passes 3/3 (same-system F1 0.52/0.46/0.42 vs null95 0.50/0.42/0.36), but the held-out-script gate fails 3/3 (F1 0.41/0.22/0.35 vs null95 0.55/0.42/0.34; base+0.10 missed). The class signal is real inside each system but does not transfer across scripts even within genre; nothing applied to Indus; Linear B dropped (only positional name labels).

tasks.title: Numerals at the end of foreign texts: pre-registered test
tasks.summary: On the 9 readings #12 accepts, 2 texts end in a numeral vs 0.28 expected from length-matched home seals (p=0.030), but both are Bahrain seals and dropping one gives p=0.24, so the preregistered rule (power 0.81 at r=0.3) calls the confirmatory test refuted. With the 11 unconfirmed readings added it is 6/20 vs 0.72 (p=5e-5, LOO 0.0006), and post hoc 6 of all 9 numeral-final foreign texts are round Gulf-type seals: treat final numerals as a Gulf-seal genre slot and keep them out of #4's name window.

tasks.title: Add the 2026 Umm al-Quwain (UAE) Indus-sign Gulf seal to the foreign corpus
tasks.summary: No primary report exists for the 2026 Umm al-Quwain Indus-sign seal: the only source (an aggregator) is now 404, and searches of UAQ/WAM, UAE dailies in English and Arabic, and the Tell Abraq mission's 2022-2025 papers find nothing; the description matches the stock Gulf Type wording. The only scholarly Umm al-Quwain seal (Abraq 2, TAD.0105, PAM 33, 2024) has no Indus signs, so 0 objects were added and the candidate is graded EXCLUDE in experiments/uaq_seal/candidate_objects.csv.

tasks.title: Real-script known-answer test of the crib attack on Linear Elamite
tasks.summary: The frozen #26 crib method, run on 224 real Linear Elamite words with a 9-name (27-30 spelling) cuneiform royal/divine crib list, recovers nothing: 0/24 cells pass, primary cell (n=45) pass share 0.00 with precision 0.13/0.03, and an equal-size Akkadian list fits as well or better in every cell. The cause is data, not search: only 2-4 of 224 words carry a crib name under the true values (15 post hoc with a spelling fix and the full 21-name list) versus the ~75% the planted gate assumed, so #4 should not be run.

tasks.title: Bench the IIT Hyderabad masked-sign restoration release (Zenodo 24164070)
tasks.summary: 107 of 296 test texts (36%) in the IIT Hyderabad restoration split have a near-copy in training; their blend scores 57.8% Hit@1 on those vs 30.5% on clean texts, so the 40.8% headline is inflated by about 10 points. On clean texts the transformer does not beat a plain trigram (28.5 vs 29.8 Hit@1, diff -1.4, 95% CI -4.0 to +1.3) and the blend gains only +0.7 (CI -1.0 to +2.3).

tasks.title: Test Dominik 2026 sharp claim: W090 follows W740 but never W520
tasks.summary: In the pre-registered order (ICIT listing order, chosen by matching the claim's denominators) the claim fails: W090 follows W520 1/160 and W740 3/1257 (p=0.93). In reading order the contrast exists (1/40 vs 90/388, p=0.0005; M77 dev 0/21 vs 57/204), mostly from Mohenjo-daro, but held-out data cannot test it (M77 held-out 0/8 vs 10/62, p=0.27) and it ranks only 18th of 57 similarly sharp sign-pair contrasts (25 at p<=0.001).

tasks.title: Red-team ivc2tyc: are Indus glyphs really closest to Tibetan-Yi scripts?
tasks.summary: TYC-over-Bronze survives style normalisation by the prereg rule (D=+0.029 [0.005,0.055]) but is carried by Ba-Shu alone; proto-cuneiform beats 3-4 of 5 TYC sets in every condition, thickening PC/PE strokes cuts D to +0.013 [-0.011,0.028], base rate 5/7, paper's t-tests pseudoreplicated.

tasks.title: Red-team #15: is the final-numeral excess on foreign texts a round Gulf-seal genre effect, a reading artefact, or real?
tasks.summary: The #15 excess is not a reading artefact (M77 readings: 11/40 numeral-final vs 2.09, p<5e-5) but sits entirely on round seals (7/23 vs 0.98, p=5e-5; non-round foreign 2/17 vs 1.1, p=0.30), and home circular seals show the same 25% rate (2/8, too few: power 0.14). Dropping the non-count signs W001/W002/W031 cuts the all-foreign result to 4 vs 1.06 (p=0.019, above alpha 0.0167), so treat final strokes as a round-seal slot, not a foreign-name feature.

tasks.title: Audit: did the 'round seal' mislabel (SEAL:R = rectangular) contaminate earlier Gulf round-seal results?
tasks.summary: No foreign object is SEAL:R, so Gulf-round headline numbers are unchanged (+2.17; grammar (d) +1.77 p=1e-4) and task #1 gets slightly stronger (9->11 of 38 flagged with the 388 rectangular seals restored to glib's reference pool). But the format control fails: true home circular/cylinder seals (n=9) are +1.84 bits/sign vs home seals (old 'home round' +0.17 was 97% rectangular) and only +0.37 below foreign round (perm p=0.48), so 'not a format effect' no longer holds (grammar scorer: home circular +0.41, p=0.18, n=12).

tasks.title: Red-team #22: are the 9-12 home circular/cylinder seals that look 'foreign' actually Gulf imports, and does the format effect survive a larger home sample?
tasks.summary: #22 survives and sharpens: corrected home round seals (n=8, Harappa tablet H-369 dropped) are off-ORDER, not off-inventory (real-vs-shuffle order +1.96 bits/sign vs home seals, Holm p=4e-4; inventory +0.16, p=0.30), and foreign round seals do not differ from them (order +0.11, p=0.68, power 0.99). KN-grammar disagreement was set membership (grammar on corrected 8: +0.96, p=0.025); 3/8 home round seals carry the Gulf-type bull (vs 4% of home seals, p=0.004) but have Indus-type bosses, so home and foreign round seals look like one Gulf-type genre.

tasks.title: Elamite personal-name crib list for #4 (syllabified, short)
tasks.summary: short_Elamite_core.csv = 50 names (mean 3.46 syllables) of men labelled 'lu2 of' Susa/Shimashki/Marhashi/Anshan/Urua/Kimash etc. in ORACC Ur III texts (83 found by a fixed rule, 33 dropped as Mesopotamian-shaped), contemporary with the Gulf seals. Unlike Sumerian/Akkadian/Amorite names, they repeat a syllable MORE than chance (24% vs null 10%, 95% 2-18%), a testable contrast for the crib attack.

tasks.title: Red-team #23: does the round-seal ORDER anomaly survive other order measures and a planted control?
tasks.summary: #23 survives a rare-sign-matched null: home round seals (n=8) keep a KN order excess of +1.64 bits/sign (Holm p=3e-4; length-only +1.92) and +0.84 under the Wells grammar (Holm p=0.02), with planted shuffles flagged 100%, rare-matched ordinary seals flagged 4.9%, leave-one-out max p 6e-4 and foreign minus home round +0.11 (p=0.66). Two corrections: positional placement is not off (+0.44, p=0.077), and the order is weak rather than absent (mean shuffle percentile 0.38 vs 0.10; only 2/8 texts at >=0.5); 5 of the 8 are round on ICIT's type code alone.

tasks.title: Redesign the crib attack so it passes a planted gate at the real sample size
tasks.summary: Exact-match crib attack with short lists, on planted CV data with the real text lengths, passes 6/36 cells, all at n>=41: a 27-spelling list passes at n=41 with no anchors (power 1.00, wrong-language FPR 0.00, precision 0.80, 47% of values recovered), lists of 66-81 spellings need n=49 plus 3-6 anchors, and the 198-spelling Akkadian list never passes. At n=9 power is 0.00-0.30 in every cell and at n=20 at most 0.70, so #17 is a go at n~45 with a <=30-spelling list while #4 on the 9-11 safe texts would be uninformative.
